description: M9 live maps provider (tasks.md T9.1-T9.2, FR-29/FR-30, AC-8). Add a real GoogleMapsLocationProvider behind the EXISTING LocationProvider Protocol, default stays HAVERSINE, needs an env API key, memoizes results in-process by (origin,dest), and falls back gracefully maps->haversine->UNKNOWN. Unknown walking must use the neutral ranking value, never zero (via the existing walking_factor_value + walking_unknown_value). Uses stdlib urllib.request for HTTP (no new dependency); tests inject a MOCKED HTTP client. DEPENDS ON nothing in FEAT-001/002/003 functionally; ordered last of the feature work. Independent of FEAT-003.
steps: In vandy_food_radar/config.py add `LocationProviderKind.GOOGLE_MAPS = "google_maps"` to the existing StrEnum. Add `@dataclass MapsConfig` with `enabled: bool = False` and `api_key: str = ""`; add `maps: MapsConfig = field(default_factory=MapsConfig)` to Config. In Config.from_env read VFR_MAPS_ENABLED (via _parse_bool) and GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY into those fields when present; default provider selection stays LocationProviderKind.HAVERSINE.

In vandy_food_radar/providers/location.py add a small HTTP seam: a `MapsHttp` Protocol with `get_json(self, url: str) -> dict | None` and a default `_UrllibMapsHttp` using urllib.request (short timeout) that returns the parsed JSON dict or None on any URLError/HTTPError/timeout/JSON error (never raises).

In vandy_food_radar/providers/location.py add `GoogleMapsLocationProvider` implementing `walking(self, origin: GeoPoint, dest: GeoPoint | None) -> WalkingResult`. Constructor: `api_key: str`, `*, http: MapsHttp | None = None`, `fallback: LocationProvider | None = None` (default HaversineLocationProvider()). Behavior: dest None -> WalkingResult(UNKNOWN); build the Distance Matrix walking-mode URL with origin/dest lat,lng + key; memoize by a rounded (origin.lat,origin.lng,dest.lat,dest.lng) tuple key in an instance dict — on a cache hit do NOT call http again; on a fresh call, http.get_json(url); parse the OK duration/distance into WalkingResult(OK, distance_m, minutes) (minutes = ceil(duration_seconds/60), min 1); on any missing key / http None / non-OK status / parse failure -> delegate to fallback.walking(origin, dest) (Haversine), and if that is UNKNOWN keep UNKNOWN. Cache the resolved WalkingResult.

Extend build_location_provider(config): when config.providers.location is LocationProviderKind.GOOGLE_MAPS AND config.maps.enabled AND config.maps.api_key present, return GoogleMapsLocationProvider(api_key=config.maps.api_key, fallback=HaversineLocationProvider()); when kind is NULL return NullLocationProvider(); otherwise return HaversineLocationProvider() (default unchanged). Update vandy_food_radar/providers/__init__.py exports to include GoogleMapsLocationProvider.

Add tests/test_location_maps.py using a FAKE MapsHttp: (a) a successful Distance Matrix response yields WalkingResult(OK) with expected minutes; (b) a second identical walking(origin,dest) call is served from cache (assert the fake http was called exactly once); (c) an http error (get_json returns None) falls back to the Haversine result (OK with a distance) for a dest with geo; (d) dest=None returns UNKNOWN and walking_factor_value(result, unknown_value=config.ranking.walking_unknown_value) returns the neutral value (0.5), never 0; (e) build_location_provider returns HaversineLocationProvider by default and GoogleMapsLocationProvider when GOOGLE_MAPS+enabled+key set.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run pytest tests/test_location_maps.py -q` passes with a MOCKED HTTP client; no live network.
GoogleMapsLocationProvider memoizes by (origin,dest): a repeated identical call does not re-invoke the HTTP client.
Graceful fallback chain maps->haversine->UNKNOWN; a missing dest yields UNKNOWN and walking_factor_value uses the neutral walking_unknown_value (never zero), matching M6 (FR-30, AC-8).
Default provider stays HAVERSINE; GoogleMapsLocationProvider is selected only when GOOGLE_MAPS + enabled + api_key present.
`make check` is green; the pre-existing 93 tests still pass.
findings: Implemented M9 live maps. config.py: added LocationProviderKind.GOOGLE_MAPS, MapsConfig(enabled=False, api_key=''), Config.maps field, and from_env reads VFR_MAPS_ENABLED (_parse_bool) + plain GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY; default location provider stays HAVERSINE. providers/location.py: added MapsHttp Protocol (get_json(url)->dict|None) and default _UrllibMapsHttp using stdlib urllib.request with a 5s timeout that returns None (never raises) on URLError/HTTPError/timeout/JSON/OS errors (no new dependency). GoogleMapsLocationProvider(api_key, *, http=None, fallback=HaversineLocationProvider()) builds the Distance Matrix walking-mode URL, memoizes by a rounded (origin.lat,lng,dest.lat,lng) tuple in an instance dict (cache hit does not re-invoke http), parses OK duration/distance into WalkingResult(OK, distance_m, minutes=ceil(seconds/60) min 1), and delegates to the Haversine fallback on missing key/http None/non-OK/parse failure; dest=None -> UNKNOWN and walking_factor_value stays neutral (0.5, never 0, FR-30/AC-8). build_location_provider returns GoogleMapsLocationProvider only when GOOGLE_MAPS + maps.enabled + api_key, NULL->NullLocationProvider, else HaversineLocationProvider (default unchanged); walking_factor_value semantics untouched. providers/__init__.py exports GoogleMapsLocationProvider. tests/test_location_maps.py (5 tests, all with a fake MapsHttp, no live network) cover success/minutes, cache single-call, http-error->haversine fallback, dest=None neutral value, and build selection. mypy strict required dict[str, object] type args on get_json and one narrow # type: ignore[index] when indexing the parsed JSON rows. Verification: `uv run pytest tests/test_location_maps.py -q` = 5 passed; `uv run mypy` = success (62 files); `make check` green with 138 tests passing (pre-existing suite unaffected).
